posts.title: 10 Questions to Ask a Custom Home Builder in Canton GA Before You Sign
posts.seoTitle: Custom Home Builder Canton GA: 10 Questions
posts.author: Sandra Watkins
posts.photoAlt: Bright kitchen with a large island in a Riverstone Homes build in North Georgia
posts.excerpt: Hiring a custom home builder in Canton GA? Ask these 10 questions first: licensing, warranty, building on your land, allowances, change orders and updates.
posts.body:
Picking a custom home builder in Canton GA is the biggest hire most families will ever make. You will talk to this company almost every week for the better part of a year, and you will live with their work for decades. So before you sign anything, ask good questions and pay attention to how they answer. Here are the ten I would ask any builder in Cherokee County, Metro Atlanta or North Georgia, including us.

1. Are you licensed in Georgia, and can I check it?

Georgia requires residential and general contractors to be licensed through the State Licensing Board for Residential and General Contractors. You can look up any builder by name or license number on the Georgia Secretary of State website in about two minutes. A good builder will hand you the number without blinking.

2. What does your written warranty cover?

Georgia law and state board rules require a written warranty on new single family homes, and the board sets the minimum. Ask to see the actual document, not a summary. Find out what is covered, for how long, and who you call when something comes up after closing.

3. Can I build on my own land?

Some builders only build in their own subdivisions. If you already own a lot, or want to buy land first, ask up front. At Riverstone, our answer is always the same: your land or ours. Here is how we build on your lot, from plans and permits to the final walk-through.

4. Who handles permits, HOA approval and site prep?

Permits, septic or sewer, grading and HOA design approval can eat weeks if nobody owns them. Ask exactly who handles each one and whether it is in the price. You should never have to chase a permit or manage subcontractors yourself.

5. Who runs the job site day to day?

Ask who your superintendent is and how often they are on site. Then ask who your main point of contact is for questions, selections and updates. Knowing names on day one beats calling a general office line in month five.

6. Can I use one of your plans, or bring my own?

A proven floor plan saves time and surprises. A custom plan gets you exactly what you want. A good builder can do either and will tell you honestly how each choice affects your budget and timeline. You can see the kinds of homes we build on our homes page.

7. What is included, and what is an allowance?

Two quotes can look the same and be thousands apart once you get to cabinets, flooring, lighting and appliances. Ask for a list of standard features and every allowance in writing, so you can compare builders apples to apples.

8. How do you handle changes after we start?

Almost everyone changes something. Ask how change orders are priced and approved, and make sure every change is in writing before the work happens.

9. How will you keep me updated?

Silence is the number one complaint people have about builders. Ask how often you will get updates and photos, and how fast they return calls and texts. Then pay attention to how quickly they answered you while you were still shopping.

10. Can I see homes you have built and talk to past buyers?

Walk a finished home if you can. Look at the trim, the doors, the porch, the little stuff. Ask for a couple of past buyers to call. Our home tour videos are a good place to start before you visit in person.

Quick answers

Do builders in Georgia need a license?

Yes. Residential and general contractors in Georgia are licensed by the state licensing board, and you can verify a license on the Georgia Secretary of State website.

Is a warranty required on a new home in Georgia?

Yes. Georgia law and board rules require a written warranty on new single family homes. Ask your builder for a copy before you sign.

Can I hire a builder if I already own land in Cherokee County?

Many builders, including Riverstone, will build on your lot. Ask about permits, site prep and utilities for your specific land early.

Shopping builders right now? We are happy to answer every one of these questions for you, no pressure. Call us at 706-514-6637 or send us a note. Your land or ours, let's find your perfect spot.

posts.title: Thinking About a Barndominium? How to Build One in Cherokee County GA
posts.seoTitle: Build a Barndominium in Cherokee County GA
posts.author: Sandra Watkins
posts.photoAlt: Loft inside a Riverstone barndominium in North Georgia with pine plank walls, iron beds and a view down to a stacked stone wall and candle chandelier
posts.photoCaption: The loft in a Riverstone barndominium build in North Georgia.
posts.excerpt: Want to build a barndominium in Cherokee County GA? What to plan for the shop and living space, county zoning and barn setbacks, and how Riverstone builds one.
posts.focusPhrase: build a barndominium in Cherokee County
posts.body:
If you have been scrolling barndo photos at 11 p.m. and sketching a shop on a napkin, you are in good company. More North Georgia families are asking us about barndominiums every month, and if you want to build a barndominium in Cherokee County or anywhere in North Georgia, this post is for you. Here is how we build them at Riverstone Homes, what to sort out before you start, and the questions I hear most.

Why barndominiums fit North Georgia so well

A barndominium puts your home and a working building under one roof. You get big open living space, a loft if you want one, and room for a shop, a boat, the tractor, tools or even animals. That combination makes a lot of sense on the kind of land we have up here: a few rolling acres outside Canton, a wooded tract near Ball Ground, or a hay field out toward Calhoun.

The photo at the top of this post is from one of our barndominium builds. Pine plank walls, a stacked stone wall, black iron chandeliers and a loft that looks down over the living room. It feels like a cabin and lives like a house. You can see more of it in the barndominium video on our videos page, and everything we offer is on our barndominiums page.

What to think through before you call a builder

The best barndo builds start with a few honest answers. Bring these to your first conversation and we will talk through each one with you.

  • How you will use the shop. Two trucks and a bass boat need a very different door and ceiling height than a woodworking bench or a couple of horses.
  • Living space. How many bedrooms and baths, and do you want a loft for the grandkids, an office or a bunk room?
  • Porches. Front, back or wrapped all the way around. In Georgia, a covered porch is basically a second living room for eight months of the year.
  • Your land. Slope, clearing, driveway, well and septic all affect cost and placement. If you are still shopping for acreage, start with our land search by county, and our post on buying land in Cherokee County GA walks through what to check before you sign.
  • Finishes. Rustic wood and stone, clean modern farmhouse, or somewhere in between.
  • Budget and financing. Get pre-approved early and plan for site costs, not just the building.

Before you build a barndominium in Cherokee County: zoning and permits

A barndominium you live in is a home, so it goes through the same residential permitting and inspections as any other house. Where people get tripped up is zoning and land use, especially if they want a separate barn or shop too.

A quick example from Cherokee County's own zoning guidance: accessory structures like detached garages, sheds and shops are covered under Section 5.6 of the county zoning ordinance, and a barn has to sit at least 75 feet from every property line. Barns in agricultural (AG) zoning get some exemptions from the standard accessory structure rules. Rules differ in Bartow, Gordon, Pickens and the cities, so we always check the exact parcel before anyone falls in love with a site plan.

This is one of those spots where having a local builder pays off. We handle permitting and site prep as part of the build, so you are not stuck on hold with the county trying to figure out which form goes where.

How Riverstone builds a barndominium, start to finish

Riverstone has been building in North Georgia since 1997, and a barndo follows the same steady process as every home we build.

  1. Building consultation. We talk through your land, budget, plan ideas and timeline before you commit to anything.
  2. Design your layout. We shape the living space and the shop around how you actually live and work.
  3. Permits and site prep. We pull permits and get the land ready to build.
  4. Construction and walk-through. Our project manager runs the job site from foundation to finish, then we walk the home with you before closing.

We build on our clients' land throughout North Metro Atlanta and North Georgia, including Cherokee, Bartow, Gordon, Whitfield, Cobb and Pickens counties. You can see how that works on our build on your land page. And if you would rather keep the shop separate from the house, we also build detached garages, workshops and pole barns to match. Take a look at everything we build in our services.

A quick word on financing

Financing matters on any build, and barndos have a wrinkle or two. Construction and barndominium loans can have different requirements than a standard mortgage, and some lenders are pickier about appraisals on barn-style homes. Talk with a lender who has done these before, get pre-approved early, and ask how they handle the shop square footage. Rates have been drifting down this fall, but they move every week, so treat any number you hear as a snapshot.

Quick answers

Can you build a barndominium on land I already own?

Yes. We build on our clients' land across North Georgia and handle permits, planning and construction from start to finish.

Do barndominiums need a building permit in Georgia?

Yes. A barndominium you live in is permitted and inspected as a home. Zoning rules for barns and accessory buildings vary by county and city, so check your exact parcel before you buy or design.

Can I add a separate shop or pole barn?

Absolutely. Along with barndominiums we build detached garages, workshops and pole barns for vehicles, tools, hay or storage.

If a barndo has been living rent free in your head for a while, let's talk it through. Call me at 770-324-3680 or send us a note. You will get honest advice from a builder who has been doing this since 1997, whether you build with us or not.
